article.title: Giving constructive feedback professionally
article.description: Useful framework: start positive, then the specific issue, then a suggestion. Phrases: 'One thing that worked really well was...', 'One area to consider improving is...', 'Going forward, it might help to...'. Avoid absolute negative language like 'this is wrong' — softer framing keeps the conversation constructive.
article.content: Useful framework: start positive, then the specific issue, then a suggestion. Phrases: 'One thing that worked really well was...', 'One area to consider improving is...', 'Going forward, it might help to...'. Avoid absolute negative language like 'this is wrong' — softer framing keeps the conversation constructive.

generated.caption:
Giving feedback can be tricky, right? To sound professional and constructive, try our simple framework: start positive, then mention the specific issue, and offer a suggestion.

Use soft phrasing; for example: "One thing that worked really well was..." then "One area to consider improving is..." and "Going forward, it might help to...". Avoid "this is wrong."

Save this for your next meeting! Follow @EnglishVault for daily English lessons!
generated.script: Logon ko feedback dete time seedha 'ye galat hai' bol dete ho kya? Ye ek bahut common mistake hai. Professional feedback ko hamesha constructive rakho, not negative. Iske liye ek simple framework hai: pehle positive point batao, jaise 'One thing that worked really well was...'. Fir, specific issue ke liye bolo, 'One area to consider improving is...'. Aur end mein solution ya suggestion do using 'Going forward, it might help to...'. Isse feedback softer lagta hai. Ab samajh aaya? Toh ab se, professional feedback ko hamesha positive se shuru karke, issue batao aur suggestion do. Absolute negative language avoid karo! Ab comment mein batao, aapko ye tip pata thi ya nahi? Aur follow karo The English Vault for more such tips!

slides.body: Giving professional feedback effectively requires a structured approach to ensure it's well-received and actionable. A useful framework involves starting with a positive observation, then addressing a specific area for improvement, and finally offering a constructive suggestion. Employ phrases like 'One thing that worked really well was...' (positive), 'One area to consider improving is...' (issue), and 'Going forward, it might help to...' (suggestion). This method replaces absolute negative language with softer framing, ensuring the conversation remains supportive and productive.
